/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh /home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/contracts/banking/account-control-agreement-first-turn-redline/scenario-02/claude-code-session/20261015-112818 'cat >> /workspace/x/note2.py <<"EOF"
head("1. Section 2 — Entitlement Orders")
sub("Section 2.1 (Pledgor countersignature) — Counter-proposal")
label("Tidewater`s change.","Deletes Tidewater`s agreement to comply with Orion`s entitlement orders “without further consent of the Pledgor,” and conditions compliance on a Pledgor countersignature until a Notice of Exclusive Control (“NEC”) has “become effective” under Section 3.")
label("Orion`s response.","We have restored the “without further consent” undertaking and the “no certification” sentence, and we accept Tidewater`s countersignature procedure in a narrowed form: until Tidewater has received an NEC, Tidewater may require a Pledgor countersignature on an Orion entitlement order as an operational verification step, unless the order is delivered with or after an NEC. The redline states expressly that this procedure does not condition Tidewater`s underlying agreement and that the parties intend Orion to have control from signing. Exhibit B has been conformed.")
label("Rationale.","We agree with Tidewater`s reading that control under UCC §8-106(d)(2) turns on what the intermediary has agreed to do, and that a springing structure is consistent with control. That analysis holds, however, only if Orion can move from the pre-NEC regime to unilateral control on its own and at once. In Tidewater`s markup Orion cannot: under §3.1, an NEC would not take effect for at least five Business Days and would never take effect if the Pledgor delivered a Cure Notice. Combined with the countersignature requirement, that gives the Pledgor a veto at every stage, which is exactly the “further consent” that §8-106(d)(2) and Credit Agreement §7.14(d) exclude. For the same reason we cannot accept the negative-consent or deemed-consent alternative described in your letter: a two-Business-Day objection right is also a Pledgor consent right. Once the NEC is immediately effective (see §3.1 below), Tidewater`s dual-authorization protocol can apply in the ordinary course without putting control at risk, and the revised §2.1 achieves that.")
sub("Section 2.2 (conflicting instructions) — Counter-proposal")
label("Tidewater`s change.","Replaces Secured Party priority with a joint-instruction rule and an open-ended right to refrain until a conflict is resolved to Tidewater`s reasonable satisfaction.")
label("Orion`s response.","An Orion order (countersigned, if delivered pre-NEC) prevails over a conflicting Pledgor order. For any conflict not resolved by that rule, we accept a bounded right to refrain before an NEC: Tidewater must notify both parties on the Business Day of receipt, may hold until the earliest of a joint instruction, an NEC or a final court order, and may not execute the conflicting Pledgor order in the meantime. There is no right to refrain from Orion orders after an NEC.")
label("Rationale.","This responds to the “maximum period” and dispute-resolution refinements your letter offered while keeping Orion`s priority intact. A refrain right that survived an NEC would be inconsistent with control and with Credit Agreement §§7.14(d) and 11.02(e).")

head("2. Section 3 — Notice of Exclusive Control")
sub("Officer`s Certificate (Section 3.1) — Accepted, as modified")
label("Tidewater`s change.","Requires an Officer`s Certificate certifying that an Event of Default has occurred and is continuing and that Orion is entitled to exercise exclusive control.")
label("Orion`s response.","Accepted in substance, in recognition of the importance Tidewater attaches to this point. Each NEC will include (or be accompanied by) a certification of an authorized officer of Orion that an Event of Default has occurred and is continuing, or that Orion is otherwise entitled under the Loan Documents to deliver the NEC. Exhibit A now contains the certification in its body, so no separate document or “Enclosure” is needed. Tidewater has no duty to inquire. As between the parties to the ACA, the accuracy of the certification is a matter solely between Orion and Halcyon and does not affect whether the NEC is effective.")
label("Rationale.","The certification gives Tidewater the written assurance and reliance protection it asked for. It cannot also become a condition that Tidewater or the Pledgor can test before the NEC takes effect, because that would bring back the consent and delay issues described above. We note that the markup text (a “duly authorized officer”) differs from your letter (an officer at Senior Vice President level or above). Orion has not agreed to an officer-level requirement, since the Administrative Agent`s authorized signatories are not all SVPs and a title test is a ground for dispute at exactly the wrong time.")
sub("Cure period, Cure Notice and Control Effective Date (Section 3.1) — Rejected")
label("Tidewater`s change.","Delays effectiveness of an NEC to five Business Days after Tidewater forwards it to the Pledgor (your letter refers to six), and makes it ineffective if the Pledgor delivers a Cure Notice.")
label("Orion`s response.","Rejected. An NEC is effective on receipt, with no cure, grace or waiting period. Tidewater will forward a copy of each NEC to the Pledgor within one Business Day, but a failure to forward does not affect effectiveness. Any claim by the Pledgor that an NEC was improperly delivered lies against Orion under the Loan Documents. Exhibit A has also been conformed. As marked up, Exhibit A still stated that “no cure period, grace period, or waiting period shall apply,” which conflicted with Tidewater`s §3.1.")
label("Rationale.","This is a firm position for Orion and the Lenders, for four reasons:")
bullet("**Control.** A mechanism under which the debtor`s notice prevents the secured party`s instruction from taking effect is a consent right. It puts perfection by control, and therefore Orion`s priority, at risk under UCC §§8-106(d)(2), 9-106 and 9-314.")
bullet("**The Loan Documents already address cure.** Whether an Event of Default exists, and any cure rights, are set out in Credit Agreement §11.01. Several defaults have no cure period at all (for example §11.01(a) and §11.01(d), which excludes any cure period for §6.09). A second, intermediary-administered cure process would override the agreed credit terms.")
bullet("**Dissipation risk.** A five-to-six Business Day window after notice to the Pledgor is when collateral is most exposed to withdrawal. It is also when a bankruptcy filing (§11.01(h)) could intervene before control is exercised.")
bullet("**The Custody Agreement does not require it.** Your letter cites Custody Agreement Section 9.3 as requiring notice to the account holder before account activity is restricted. The Custody Agreement we have (including Amendment No. 1 dated September 15, 2023) has no Section 9.3; Article IX consists of Sections 9.1 (indemnification) and 9.2 (survival). In any event, Halcyon is a party to the ACA and consents to the NEC mechanics, and §§11.2 and 21.1 give the ACA precedence. If there is a further amendment or side letter we have not seen, please send it to us. Halcyon has represented in Pledge and Security Agreement §4.05 that the Custody Agreement has not been amended except as disclosed.")
body("For the same reasons, Orion cannot accept the three-Business-Day alternative or a cure mechanism limited to particular categories of default.")
sub("Section 3.3 (conclusive reliance) — Accepted, as modified")
body("Orion accepts Tidewater`s conclusive-reliance and no-investigation language for the Officer`s Certificate, which is consistent with the Orion Form`s existing no-inquiry protection. The reference to a Cure Notice has been deleted because no cure mechanism remains.")
EOF

/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh /home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/contracts/banking/account-control-agreement-first-turn-redline/scenario-02/claude-code-session/20261015-112818 'cat >> /workspace/x/note2.py <<"EOF"
head("3. Section 4 — Subordination of Securities Intermediary`s Lien")
sub("Sections 4.1–4.3 (Custodian Lien) — Counter-proposal")
label("Tidewater`s change.","Reserves an uncapped Custodian Lien, senior to Orion`s security interest, for Custodial Fees, Expenses and Overdraft Advances. It also permits set-off on 10 Business Days` notice and allows Tidewater to look to the Account for all Custodian Obligations.")
label("Orion`s response.","Orion accepts the principle of a fee carve-out and consents to it for purposes of Credit Agreement §8.02 and Schedule 8.02, within the parameters your letter identified as open for discussion:")
bullet("**Covered obligations.** The senior Custodian Lien secures unpaid Custodial Fees and Expenses (as defined in the Custody Agreement, including standard transaction and settlement charges under its fee schedule) that are attributable to the Account and incurred in the ordinary course. As your letter offered, Overdraft Advances are excluded. So are interest, extraordinary Expenses and amounts relating to other accounts. These remain claims against Halcyon, but they are subordinated to Orion.")
bullet("**Priority Cap.** The lien is senior only up to $175,000 at any time outstanding. That is a full year of the approximately $175,000 annual fees your letter projects, against fees that are billed and payable quarterly in arrears under Custody Agreement §5.1(b). Amounts above the cap are subordinated.")
bullet("**Set-off (§4.2).** We accept the 10-Business-Day notice period, which matches Custody Agreement §5.4(b). The notice must specify the amounts and the assets to be applied. Set-off may not proceed if the past-due amount is paid during the notice period (Orion may pay but is not obliged to), and cash must be applied before Financial Assets are liquidated, as Custody Agreement §5.4(b) already requires.")
bullet("**Section 4.3.** Outside the capped Custodian Lien, Tidewater looks solely to Halcyon and its unencumbered assets, and will not assert any claim against Orion for fees. The “irrevocably” language of the Orion Form has been restored.")
label("Rationale.","Credit Agreement §7.14(f) permits exceptions to subordination only as Orion agrees, and Schedule 8.02 requires express written consent to any senior intermediary lien. A capped carve-out for the ordinary-course fees that maintain the collateral is the market accommodation. An uncapped senior lien that includes discretionary credit extensions is not. We understand that a narrower carve-out will need re-approval by Ms. Langston, and we are happy to discuss the cap figure with her directly. sub("Section 5.1 (statement frequency and timing) — Accepted, as modified")
label("Orion`s response.","Orion accepts monthly statements. label("Rationale.","This follows your letter`s concern about custom programming. label("Orion`s response.","Rather than reinstating real-time access within five Business Days, new §5.4 requires commercially reasonable efforts to give Orion read-only access for up to two designated users within 90 days, through the Tidewater ClientView Portal (the portal defined in Custody Agreement §4.2(c); your letter refers to “TidewaterDirect”). body("Orion accepts the waiver and has made it mutual, as your letter offered. Two adjustments are made. /home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh /home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/contracts/banking/account-control-agreement-first-turn-redline/scenario-02/claude-code-session/20261015-112818 'cat >> /workspace/x/note2.py <<"EOF"
head("6. Section 8 — Indemnification")
sub("Sections 8.1–8.3 — Counter-proposal")
label("Tidewater`s change.","Makes the Secured Party jointly and severally liable with the Pledgor for a broadened indemnity (including all claims relating to “this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby”), with a gross-negligence/willful-misconduct carve-out. It also deletes Orion Form §8.2.")
label("Orion`s response.","Orion rejects joint and several liability and accepts the bifurcated structure your letter proposed:")
bullet("**§8.1 (Pledgor).** Halcyon remains the primary indemnitor for clauses (b) through (d) as Tidewater drafted them (including third-party claims relating to the Account). Clause (a) is narrowed to Pledgor breaches, as your letter invited. Clauses (b) and (c) are tied to instructions and performance “in accordance with this Agreement.”")
bullet("**New §8.2 (Secured Party).** Orion indemnifies Tidewater for losses arising directly from Tidewater`s compliance, in accordance with the ACA, with Orion`s own entitlement orders or NECs. This applies only to the extent Halcyon has not paid within 30 days of demand, and not for losses caused by Tidewater`s negligence, bad faith or willful misconduct. Orion`s obligation is several, not joint, and excludes Pledgor-originated instructions, Custody Agreement matters and fees.")
bullet("**§8.3 (Tidewater).** Renumbered and conformed to the §6.1 standard.")
label("Rationale.","Orion acts as Administrative Agent for a syndicate. It does not accept open-ended, joint and several exposure for the custodial relationship between Tidewater and its client. Tidewater`s stated objective is recourse to the party whose instructions give rise to the claim, and the limited §8.2 provides exactly that. The carve-out must follow the liability standard in §6.1, which, as noted, is the negligence standard Tidewater already accepts in Custody Agreement §9.1.")

head("7. Section 10.3 — Termination by Tidewater")
sub("Counter-proposal")
label("Tidewater`s change.","Unilateral termination on 30 days` notice. On termination, assets are to be transferred “in accordance with the Custody Agreement and the instructions of the Pledgor” unless an NEC is in effect.")
label("Orion`s response.","Orion accepts that Tidewater may resign, but on the following terms:")
bullet("**Notice.** 90 days` notice, which is the period in Custody Agreement §12.3 for Tidewater`s own termination of the custody relationship. (Your letter cites a 60-day right in §12.2, but that is the Client`s termination right.) A shorter period, of not less than 30 days unless law requires less, applies where continued performance would breach law, Sanctions or a regulatory directive. This reflects the for-cause concept your letter suggested.")
bullet("**Effectiveness.** Resignation takes effect only once the assets have been transferred to a successor intermediary designated by Orion (in consultation with Halcyon) under a replacement control agreement. Orion will use commercially reasonable efforts to designate a successor during the notice period. If none is designated, Tidewater`s duties narrow to safekeeping and complying with Orion`s orders.")
bullet("**No transfer to the Pledgor.** In no event will assets be released to Halcyon or anyone other than the successor without Orion`s order or countersignature. Tidewater may retain capped Custodian Obligations as provided in §4.")
label("Rationale.","As drafted in the markup, a Tidewater notice would end Orion`s control and send the collateral to the Pledgor after 30 days. That would trigger Credit Agreement §§6.02(f), 11.01(l) and 11.01(m), and would be at odds with Exhibit E to the Credit Agreement, which contemplates termination only with the Administrative Agent`s consent. The revised §10.3 gives Tidewater the exit right its Legal and Compliance Committee requires while keeping the collateral under control until it is moved. We note also that your letter describes transfer to a successor designated by the Secured Party, which is closer to Orion`s counter-proposal than to the markup text.")

head("8. Section 12 and Related Provisions — Governing Law; Jurisdiction")
sub("Section 12.1, Section 1.4, the “UCC” definition and Schedule A — Counter-proposal")
label("Tidewater`s change.","Maryland governing law, Maryland UCC throughout, and Maryland as the securities intermediary`s jurisdiction.")
label("Orion`s response.","We accept the compromise your letter proposed. New York law governs the ACA as a contract (with General Obligations Law §§5-1401 and 5-1402 restored). Maryland is designated as the securities intermediary`s jurisdiction under UCC §8-110(e) in §1.4 and Schedule A, consistent with Custody Agreement §§2.2(b) and 14.1. Section 12.1 acknowledges that Maryland law governs the matters in §8-110(b) and the perfection, effect of perfection and priority of Orion`s security interest. The “UCC” definition follows the Credit Agreement formulation: New York UCC, with the Maryland UCC applying where it governs perfection or priority. Tidewater and Halcyon also agree not to change the jurisdiction designation in the Custody Agreement without Orion`s consent. As a technical correction, the reference in §1.4 to “Section 8-110(d)” has been corrected to §8-110(b), the subsection that lists the matters governed by the law of the intermediary`s jurisdiction.")
label("Rationale.","Credit Agreement §7.14(g) requires New York governing law for the ACA, so a change in contractual governing law is not available to Orion. We agree with Tidewater that the ACA and the Custody Agreement should designate the same intermediary`s jurisdiction, to avoid any uncertainty about the law governing perfection and priority. Orion`s agreement to the Maryland designation is subject to delivery at closing of a customary opinion of Halcyon`s counsel covering perfection and control under the Maryland UCC (Credit Agreement §7.01(e)). We are coordinating that with Halcyon.")
sub("Section 12.2 (forum) — Counter-proposal")
body("Submission to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of both the New York courts (S.D.N.Y. and New York County Supreme Court) and the Maryland courts (D. Md. and the Baltimore City courts). This is one of the alternatives your letter proposed and ensures that Tidewater is never compelled to litigate exclusively outside Maryland. §12.3 operates unchanged against the courts listed in §12.2. We have also added Baltimore bank holidays to the “Business Day” definition so that the processing periods in §15.3 track Tidewater`s operating days.")

head("9. Section 14.1(e) — No Other Control Agreements")
sub("Rejected; counter-proposal")
label("Orion`s response.","The representation is restored as new §14.1(e), with the remaining clauses re-lettered (f) and (g). As your letter offered, the representation is qualified, for agreements or authorizations predating the ACA only, by Tidewater`s knowledge after due inquiry of its account records and of the Institutional Custody Services officers responsible for the Account. It is paired with a covenant to notify Orion promptly if Tidewater becomes aware of any such agreement. Section 11.1, which contains the same representation and which Tidewater did not mark, has been conformed so the two provisions are consistent.")
label("Rationale.","The acknowledgment is an express requirement of Credit Agreement §7.14(e) and Exhibit E. It concerns agreements to which Tidewater itself would be a party, and Tidewater is better placed than anyone to give it. The Pledgor`s lien representation in §14.2 does not substitute for it. The knowledge qualifier addresses the legacy-records concern in your letter.")
sub("Conforming changes (Sections 14.1(b), 14.1(g) and 14.2(e))")
body("References to the “subordinated lien” of Tidewater have been conformed to refer to its lien as described in, and subject to, Section 4 (including the capped Custodian Lien).")

head("10. Section 15.3 — Timing of Compliance")
sub("Counter-proposal")
label("Tidewater`s change.","Commercially reasonable efforts to act on entitlement orders and NECs within two Business Days, with a safe harbor whenever such efforts were used.")
label("Orion`s response.","")
bullet("**NECs.** An NEC, which requires Tidewater only to stop acting on Pledgor instructions, must be implemented immediately on receipt, and in any event the same Business Day if received before cut-off (otherwise by the opening of business on the next Business Day).")
bullet("**Entitlement orders.** Tidewater will use commercially reasonable efforts to execute on the day of receipt, which is the commitment Tidewater already gives Halcyon in Custody Agreement §6.3(a). Outside dates are one Business Day for cash orders and two Business Days for securities orders (customary settlement cycle for non-U.S., sub-custodian or transfer-agent settlements). This follows the tiered approach your letter proposed.")
bullet("**Safe harbor.** Accepted, but limited to delays caused by Force Majeure Events, legally required authentication and sanctions/AML screening conducted diligently and with prompt notice to Orion, or failures of counterparties, depositories or settlement systems, in each case where Tidewater used commercially reasonable efforts.")
bullet("**Cut-off times.** The cut-off-time mechanics of the Orion Form have been restored.")
label("Rationale.","A two-Business-Day window for an NEC would leave the Pledgor free to direct the Account after control has been exercised, and the delay that matters most is the delay in freezing Pledgor activity. Your letter cites Custody Agreement Section 4.5 for a two-Business-Day standard. We do not find a Section 4.5 in the Custody Agreement; the relevant provision, §6.3(a), provides for same-day execution on a commercially-reasonable-efforts basis. We recognize Tidewater`s concern about compressing compliance screening, and the safe harbor expressly protects legally required screening.")

head("11. Exhibits A and B")
body("Exhibit A now contains the Officer`s Certificate language and states that the NEC is effective on receipt. The free-standing “Enclosure” line has been deleted. In Exhibit B, the countersignature block is retained but limited to orders delivered before an NEC, and the “[ADDED: …]” drafting placeholder has been removed.")
EOF
echo ok'

  - Set-off on 10 business days' notice is accepted, with conditions.

- **§6 liability:**
  - Standard of care is negligence, matching Custody Agreement §§7.1 and 8.1(a); gross negligence applies to reporting only.
  - Direct damages are accepted and defined to include collateral wrongly released.
  - The consequential damages waiver is made mutual, with carve-outs.
  - The cap becomes the greater of 12 months' fees and $2.5M, with carve-outs.
- **§8 indemnity:** joint and several liability is rejected. Halcyon is the primary indemnitor; Orion gives a limited, several, secondary indemnity (Tidewater's own suggested alternative).
- **§10.3 termination (counter):** 90 days' notice (shorter where law requires). It takes effect only once the assets move to a successor intermediary, and assets never go to the Pledgor.
- **§12 governing law (counter):** New York law is kept (Credit Agreement §7.14(g)), with GOL §§5-1401/1402 restored. Maryland is accepted as the intermediary's jurisdiction for UCC §8-110(e) purposes, which is Tidewater's proposed split. Courts are non-exclusive New York and Maryland.
- **§14.1(e) "no other control agreements" (deletion rejected):** the representation is restored with a knowledge qualifier for pre-signing agreements and a notice covenant; §11.1 is conformed to match.
- **§15.3 timing:** a notice must be complied with the same day. Orders run on tiers (cash 1 business day, securities 2) with a narrowed safe harbor.
- **Exhibits:** conformed. Tidewater's "[ADDED: …]" placeholder is removed, and the leftover "no cure period" line in their Exhibit A is fixed.

**Errors in Tidewater's cover letter, which the note points out:**
- Custody Agreement §8.1 is a negligence standard, not gross negligence.
- Custody §8.2 caps liability at the greater of fees and $1M.
- Tidewater's own termination right is §12.3 on 90 days; §12.2 is the client's 60-day right.
- There is no Custody §9.3 or §4.5. §6.3(a) actually commits to same-day execution.
- The portal is named "Tidewater ClientView Portal", not "TidewaterDirect".
- In several places the letter describes terms that differ from the markup text.
- The email addresses in their letter and email differ from each other and from Schedule B. The note goes to every version and asks them to confirm.

**Decisions for you or Orion to confirm before this goes out:**
- **Opening numbers.** The $175,000 lien cap and $2.5M liability cap are opening figures I chose; nothing in the documents sets them.
- **Maryland jurisdiction.** Accepting Maryland as the intermediary's jurisdiction is conditioned on a closing opinion from Halcyon's counsel on perfection under Maryland's UCC.
- **Termination.** Allowing Tidewater to resign departs from Credit Agreement Exhibit E, which contemplates termination only with Orion's consent.
- **Tidewater's cc.** Their letter copied Priya Chandrasekaran "per instruction of Whitfield Greer". I left this unaddressed; please check whether that instruction was given.
- **Dates and call times.** I dated the note May 9, 2025 and proposed call slots for May 13–15 with a May 16 response date. All of these are placeholders.
